user.text: When navigating from the dashboard to a project, I want the project's title to appear instantly, but I don't want to prefetch the rest of the project page.

history.assistant:
I made the change, and `npx next build` passes (exit 0) with `/projects/[slug]` built as a Partial Prerender. I haven't checked in a running production app (prefetching only runs in production) that the title arrives with the prefetch and the details don't.

The title comes from the URL's `slug`, so a normal prefetch can't include it. Instead, each dashboard link now does its own prefetch that works out the slug and loads the cached title. The rest of the project page is marked to load only when you actually navigate.

- **`next.config.ts`**: added `partialPrefetching: true`. This is needed because without it, `prefetch={true}` fetches the whole page, including the parts meant to load later.
- **`app/page.tsx`**: the project links now use `<Link prefetch={true}>`.
- **`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`**: I split the page into two parts, each with its own loading placeholder:
  - `ProjectTitle` reads `params` and calls `getProjectTitle`, which is already cached. This is what the link prefetches, so the title shows as soon as you click.
  - `ProjectDetails` calls `await navigation()` first, so the slow `getProjectDetails` call (800ms) isn't prefetched. Only its "Loading details..." placeholder is, and the details stream in after you click.

The build also edited `tsconfig.json` on its own: it set `jsx` to `react-jsx` and added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`.

tool_steps.assistant: I'll inspect the app structure and the local Next.js docs on prefetching/loading to find the right approach.
